headline: Competitive Yawning League Announces New 'Contagion Division' Amid Expansion
subheadline: Athletes who can trigger chain yawns in audiences command highest salaries
summary: The World Yawning Federation is expanding its competitive categories as the sport gains mainstream traction.
content:
The World Yawning Federation (WYF) has announced the addition of a "Contagion Division" to its competitive roster, where athletes are judged not just on yawn quality but on their ability to trigger involuntary yawns in live audiences.

"Pure yawning is about form and duration," explained WYF Commissioner Bethany Yates. "Contagion yawning is about power. These athletes don't just yawn—they weaponize it. They make you yawn. You can't stop yourself. That's the art."

The new division will debut at the 2026 World Championships, where competitors will perform before live audiences while sensors track how many spectators involuntarily yawn in response. Current frontrunner Marcus "The Maw" Williams holds the record for inducing 847 sympathetic yawns in a single three-minute routine.

"I've been training since childhood," Williams said during a press conference, punctuating his remarks with a demonstration yawn that caused three reporters to yawn visibly. "Sorry. Can't turn it off. It's a gift and a curse."

The sport has categories for different yawn styles: the "Slow Build" (extended approach), the "Sneak Attack" (sudden full extension), the "Vocal" (audible exhalation), and the controversial "Jaw Crack" division, which some critics consider extreme.

Skeptics have questioned whether competitive yawning qualifies as athletic competition. The WYF points to the physical demands of jaw muscle control and the mental discipline required to yawn on command without genuine fatigue.

"Try yawning right now," challenged athlete Sandra "The Stretch" DeLuca. "Really try. Can you? Most people can't summon it at will. We've trained our bodies to yawn whenever, wherever. That's not nothing."

The league's Threadit community, r/CompetitiveYawning, has 847,000 members who debate technique and share training tips. Common advice includes "watch videos of other people yawning" and "embrace your tiredness."

Dr. Helena Ross, a sleep researcher, called the phenomenon "fascinating from a neurological perspective. Contagious yawning relates to empathy and social bonding. These athletes are essentially competing at being relatable."

Tickets for the World Championships sold out in minutes. Attendees are warned to expect drowsiness.
author: Tom Hendricks, Sports Reporter
